messages:
Maya (PM): Quick sync request: ACME wants a "session-buckets" model for dedicated pools where capacity is described as concurrent session-buckets (not tokens). They also asked for a "soft borrow" feature so product teams can temporarily borrow unused reserved capacity from the pool and repay with burst-credit adjustments. They want the ability to rollover unused credits monthly. Thoughts on MVP scope?

Nikhil (eng-platform): Session-buckets makes sense for chat-heavy apps. Need to define bucket semantics: 1 bucket = 1 concurrent session up to N tokens per minute? Or variable sized?

Jules (eng-runtime): We should standardize: 1 session-bucket = concurrent websocket/chat session with up to 512 tokens/sec baseline. Anything above that consumes extra credit. That keeps admission simple.

Devon (solutions): ACME will want per-team visibility and an emergency borrow flow for product launches. They care about predictable P95 latency during market open. Rollover helps them not waste monthly commit.

Priya (sales): They're willing to accept a small premium for borrow capability + rollover. But they need clear guardrails to avoid resource hogging.

Riley (cust-success): Compliance ask: audit trail for borrows + automatic email notifications for borrow events and repayment. Also revocation must be immediate.

Nikhil (eng-platform): Potential guardrail idea: soft-borrow = ephemeral borrow up to X% of pool capacity, borrowed capacity must be repaid within Y hours or consumed by burning burst credits (configurable). Borrow requests trigger an alert to pool admins.

Jules (eng-runtime): Autoscale interaction: autoscale should still react to real-time pool concurrency. Borrow should not force scale-up; it's an admission overlay. If borrow consistently pushes utilization high, autoscale will scale the pool normally.

Maya (PM): For MVP I recommend these constraints:
- Session-bucket defined as Jules suggested (concurrency unit + baseline token allowance)
- Soft-borrow allowed up to 20% of pool capacity and time-limited (max 48 hours)
- Borrow repayment options: repay by returning sessions, or automatic credit deduction based on negotiated rate
- Monthly rollover of up to 25% unused burst credits to next billing period
- UI to request/approve borrows + audit logs + email hooks

Devon (solutions): Recommend also a simulator for customers to model borrow scenarios. For POC we can do CSV exports with projected borrow burn and latency impact.

Priya (sales): ACME timeline: POC in 5 weeks, GA in 12-13 weeks if POC looks clean. They want a short demo of sim outputs.

Nikhil (eng-platform): Engineering estimate for MVP: platform infra + credit engine tweaks (3w), runtime admission & borrow enforcement (3w), UI + approval flow + billing (2w), test/soak + docs (2w) => ~10w. Tight but doable.

Jules (eng-runtime): API sketch for borrow flow (rough):
```
POST /v1/dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/borrow_requests
{
  "requester_subtenant": "acme.payments.frontend",
  "requested_buckets": 30,
  "duration_hours": 12,
  "repayment_mode": "auto-credit-deduction", // or "manual-return"
  "justification":"prod-launch A/B rollout",
  "notify_approvers": ["ops@acme.com"]
}
```

Maya (PM): Add "max_borrow_percent" and "approval_required" fields on pool config. Also need API for approved borrows listing + revoke token.

Riley (cust-success): Acceptance criteria from customer POV:
- Borrow requests appear in UI within 5s
- Borrow approval/denial action audited and emailed
- Rollover and credit burn line items visible in billing export
- Latency SLO (P95) maintained within 10% of baseline during approved borrows for market hours

Nikhil (eng-platform): Ops acceptance criteria:
- Alerts when borrowed capacity > threshold (e.g., 10%)
- Ability to forcibly revoke borrows and drain sessions gracefully
- Strongly consistent ledger for credits/balances (reads) around repayment window

Jules (eng-runtime): Test plan notes: simulate 50% of pool idle then sudden concurrent borrows from 3 subtenants, verify admission, verify autoscale reacts only if sustained, verify repayment deduction accuracy < 1%. Also measure fallback behavior for overcommit (fallback to hosted variant).

Maya (PM): Non-MVP items to call out: cross-pool borrowing, delegated preemption, dynamic bucket resizing, fine-grained per-minute billing for mid-session overages. We'll table those.

Priya (sales): I'll negotiate POC terms: telemetry access for 3 weeks and ability to run synthetic load. Ask them to accept fallback to hosted variant for overcommit during POC.

Devon (solutions): We'll prepare a short sim harness and CSV export for ACME that projects borrow burn and cost. Plan: simple CSV with columns: minute, concurrent_sessions, predicted_burn, projected_latency.

ops-bot: Created TASK-736 "session-buckets + soft-borrow MVP" assigned to Maya, due_date=2025-07-18. :spiral_calendar:

Maya (PM): Owners + short ETAs:
- Pool config schema + API: Maya + Nikhil 9(4d)
- Runtime borrow enforcement + session-bucket defs: Jules (3w)
- Credits engine (rollover + repayment): Nikhil + billing eng (3w)
- UI + approval workflow: Devon + UI eng (2w)
- Customer sim export: Devon (1w)
- SRE runbook + alerts: Nikhil + Riley (1.5w)

Riley (cust-success): I'll draft the audit checklist and email templates for notifications.

Jules (eng-runtime): I'll include a small migration plan: existing pools get implicit bucket mapping; new pools opt-in to session-buckets. No automatic migration for safety.

Maya (PM): Decisions recorded:
- Adopt session-bucket unit (1 concurrent session up to 512 tokens/sec)
- Implement time-limited soft-borrow (max 20% pool cap, 48h) with repayment modes
- Allow monthly rollover up to 25% of unused burst credits
- Autoscale remains pool-driven; borrow is admission overlay
- UI + audit + email + simulator for onboarding

Priya (sales): I'll flag to ACME that we support rollover and soft-borrow in the POC ask.

Nikhil (eng-platform): Note: will implement strong consistency for credit ledger during repayment windows; other reads can be eventual. Documented in design doc.

Maya (PM): Let's regroup in 3 days after the API/ schema draft. Flag any major blockers now.

Priya (sales): ack, will coordinate ACME access.

Maya (PM): End thread. Thanks everyone.
